svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.6.1 Obstructions by Doors
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Obstructions by Doors

g.text: Fully open: takes not more than 100 mm
During its swing: the path left is not less
than the required width of the exit corridor
Exit doors and doors into a public
corridor or other access to exit
PLANS: THE SWING OF A DOOR LEAF

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Obstructions created by doors are limited by
Sentences (2) and (3) at
(a) exit doors, (b) doors that open into or are
located within a public corridor, and (c) doors
that open into or are located within another
facility that provides access to exit from a
suite. Except as provided in Sentence (4).
When fully open, these doors do not decrease
the required exit width by more than
(a) 100 mm (3 15/16″) in exit corridors, and (b)
50 mm (1 15/16″) for other exit facilities.
The swing of these doors does not reduce the
width of the path of travel to less than
(a) the required exit width in exit corridors and
passageways, and (b) 750 mm (29½″) on exit stairs
or landings.
Doors serving a single dwelling unit need not
comply with Sentences (2) and (3)
Drawn: a door into an exit corridor, shown fully open (solid) and at 90 degrees (dashed). Plans not to scale.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.6.1. (page 9-48)
